fixes.explanation: Hebron never comes up in this passage, friend. Verse 7 says David took the gold shields that belonged to Hadadezer's officers and brought them to Jerusalem. Picture those officers with their shiny gold shields, and then David just walks off with them. I think those officers had a very quiet walk home.

Gibeon isn't in this passage, baker. The text says David brought the gold shields of Hadadezer's officers to Jerusalem (2 Samuel 8:7). Those officers owned gold shields, and then David carried them off. That's a rough day at work for them.

A treaty isn't mentioned here, baker. Verse 13 says David made a name for himself when he returned from striking down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt. Nobody signs anything in that verse. It reads more like word got around, and I think a lot of folks heard his name.
